facet_selection_reasoning: This combination tests the student's understanding of the Central Limit Theorem and sampling distribution properties. It contrasts the correct understanding that larger sample sizes reduce standard error and approach normality (A1, A2) with the common misconception that the sampling distribution is always normal regardless of sample size or population distribution shape (B12).

item.stem: Consider a population that is heavily skewed. Researchers are investigating the sampling distribution of the sample mean (x̄) as the sample size (n) increases. Which of the following accurately describes how the sampling distribution changes as n increases?

options.text: The sampling distribution becomes more normally distributed, and the spread of the distribution decreases because the standard error gets smaller.
options.rationale: Correctly identifies that as sample size increases, the Central Limit Theorem causes the distribution to approach normality (A2) and the variability/standard error decreases (A1).

options.text: The sampling distribution always follows a normal distribution regardless of the sample size.
options.rationale: This reflects the misconception that the sampling distribution is always normal, ignoring that normality is an asymptotic property dependent on sufficient sample size (B12).

options.text: The sampling distribution becomes more normally distributed, but the spread of the distribution remains constant regardless of the sample size.
options.rationale: Correctly identifies the move toward normality but incorrectly assumes the spread (standard error) remains constant, which confuses the sampling distribution with the population (B9).

options.text: The sampling distribution always maintains the same shape as the population distribution, so it remains skewed regardless of the sample size.
options.rationale: This reflects the misconception that the sampling distribution mirrors the population distribution shape rather than approaching normality (B11).

item.explanation: This item tests the students' understanding of the Central Limit Theorem. It requires them to differentiate between the shape of the sampling distribution as it approaches normality (A2) and the reduction in standard error (variability) as sample size increases (A1), while specifically acting as a distractor for those who believe the distribution is inherently or always normal regardless of sample size (B12).
